unusual_experiment.reason: No immutable shared request/turn id and no reproducible whole-second trigger timestamp were available.

finding.summary: The reserved autonomous terminal transport prefix could fall through to the ordinary human UserPromptSubmit path when its nonce was malformed, wrong, expired, missing, or already consumed.
finding.mechanism: consume_dispatch_prompt returned None for reserved-prefix failures; terminal_hooks.user_prompt interprets None as ordinary human input. That can misclassify a synthetic autonomy marker as a human turn and can contaminate the later human-roundtrip attestation used by AutonomyPulse.
finding.strongest_counterhypothesis: A reserved-prefix miss is harmless because it contains no stored autonomy instruction. This is rejected at the authority/provenance boundary: even without the instruction, admitting the synthetic marker as a human turn falsifies provenance and can satisfy a human-attestation predicate that checks canonical hook provenance rather than transport origin.

delta: Treat __CLAY_AUTONOMY_DISPATCH__: as a reserved transport namespace.
Ordinary non-prefixed human text still returns None and follows the human path.
Malformed reserved nonce, missing lease, nonce mismatch, expired lease, and replay now raise AutonomyDispatchError fail-closed.
Generation, goal/step, lease generation, and one-shot deletion fences remain unchanged.
Focused tests now require fail-closed reserved-prefix behavior while preserving ordinary human text handling.
next_discriminator: Execute the exact candidate dispatch tests plus terminal hook/autonomy pulse adjacency in an authorized isolated full checkout; then prove a stale/expired/replayed synthetic terminal marker cannot create a canonical human turn or satisfy the human-roundtrip pulse attestation.
